cases.question: Is Zapme any good, and what do people say about it?
cases.answer_text:
Assuming you mean **Zapme: eSIM & Global Numbers**: **it looks legitimate, but I’d treat it as “promising, not proven.”** I wouldn’t call it a scam from what I found, but there isn’t enough independent feedback for me to confidently say it’s one of the best eSIM options.

**What people say:**

- **iPhone users are very positive, but the sample is tiny.** The AU App Store shows **4.8/5 from only 17 ratings**. Reviews praise cheaper roaming, convenience, global numbers, and having eSIM + calling/text/video features in one app. ([apps.apple.com](https://apps.apple.com/au/app/zapme-esim-global-numbers/id6471850240))  
- **Android feedback is much more mixed.** Google Play shows about **3.2/5 from ~130 reviews** and **50K+ downloads**; positive reviews mention ease of use, decent pricing, and useful 30‑day/global-number features. ([play.google.com](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?hl=en-US&id=com.zapme.zapme_mobile.prod1&utm_source=openai))  
- **Complaints/concerns I’d take seriously:** a third-party review summary flags issues like unclear pricing before proceeding, trouble deleting accounts, some country-number display issues, international calling limitations, and isolated privacy concerns. ([chrome-stats.com](https://chrome-stats.com/d/com.zapme.zapme_mobile.prod1/reviews?utm_source=openai))  
- **Travel-forum chatter is cautious rather than enthusiastic.** On Australian Frequent Flyer, someone asked about Zapme and the reply was basically: it appears to focus on global roaming / long-duration plans, which can be convenient across multiple countries but often costs more than country- or region-specific eSIMs. ([australianfrequentflyer.com.au](https://www.australianfrequentflyer.com.au/community/threads/esims-what-is-your-experience.104542/page-55))  
- **One odd red flag:** Zapme’s own Australia/NZ page had “What People Are Saying” testimonials showing “John Doe” and lorem-ipsum placeholder text, which doesn’t inspire confidence in their marketing polish. ([zapme.co](https://zapme.co/esim-australia-new-zealand/))  
- **Privacy-wise, read the permissions carefully.** Apple’s App Store privacy section says location may be used for tracking, and Google Play says the app may share personal info and collect personal/financial data and other data types. ([apps.apple.com](https://apps.apple.com/au/app/zapme-esim-global-numbers/id6471850240))  

**My verdict:**  
Zapme may be worth trying **if you specifically want one app for eSIM data + virtual/global numbers + long-duration/monthly use**, especially for multi-country travel. But if you just need cheap travel data for one country or region, I’d compare it against Airalo, Nomad, Ubigi, Eskimo, Trip.com eSIMs, or a local prepaid eSIM first—Zapme doesn’t yet have the volume of trusted, independent reviews that bigger eSIM providers do.

**If you do use it:** buy the smallest one-month plan first, test activation before departure, check refund/support terms, confirm your phone is unlocked and eSIM-compatible, and don’t rely on it as your only connectivity option for a critical trip.

cases.question: Is Zapme any good, and what do people say about it?
cases.answer_text:
**Zapme** is an app-based "communications superapp" designed for global travelers, digital nomads, and remote workers. Unlike traditional eSIM apps that only provide local data, Zapme offers a unified platform where you can purchase **both eSIM data plans and virtual global phone numbers** (mobile, landline, and toll-free) that you can manage on a single device. 

Overall, **Zapme is considered a highly useful, niche tool—especially if you need to receive SMS verification codes while abroad**. However, it is still a relatively young service, and users have reported some minor technical and customer support complaints. 

---

### What Makes Zapme Good? (The Pros)

* **All-in-One eSIM & Phone Numbers:** Most eSIM apps are data-only, meaning you have to rely on WhatsApp or FaceTime for calls. Zapme lets you buy real virtual numbers from different countries and manage them through one eSIM profile.
* **Crucial for 2FA and OTPs:** One of Zapme’s standout features is its ability to **receive international SMS**. This is incredibly valuable for travelers and remote workers who need to receive One-Time Passwords (OTPs) to log into banking, government, or social media accounts while abroad.
* **Persistent Identity:** You can buy a number and keep it long-term. This gives you a consistent caller ID and a reliable way for clients or banks to reach you, no matter where you travel.
* **Flexible, No-Contract Plans:** Zapme operates on a prepaid, month-to-month subscription model (with packages like *Just GO*, *Sweet SPOT*, and *The MOON*). There are no lock-in contracts, and you can cancel at any time.
* **Reasonable Pricing:** Plans and numbers are quite affordable, often starting around $4.50 to $4.95, with robust monthly packages around £14.99 ($19). 

---

### What Do People Critique? (The Cons)

* **Mixed App Ratings Between Stores:** While Zapme has a high rating on the Apple App Store (around 4.8/5, though based on fewer reviews), its ratings on Google Play are more average (around 3.2 to 3.6/5). Android users have reported more frequent bugs and occasional UI glitches.
* **Account Deletion Issues:** Some users have expressed frustration over the app's lack of a straightforward way to delete user accounts directly in the settings.
* **Limited Number Availability:** Depending on when you check, virtual numbers for certain countries (such as Germany) may be listed as "coming soon" or unavailable.
* **Web3/ICO Components Can Feel Unnecessary:** Zapme’s founders have positioned the app as a bridge between Web2 and Web3, incorporating features like decentralized messaging and rewards tokens. For everyday travelers who just want a working phone number, these crypto/Web3 elements can feel confusing or unnecessary.
* **Network Performance Fluctuations:** As with any eSIM provider, Zapme relies on local roaming partners. Depending on the country you land in, your speeds (4G vs. 5G) and coverage can vary.

---

### The Verdict: Is Zapme Right For You?

* **You should get Zapme if:** You travel frequently, work remotely, or run an international business and **need to maintain a virtual phone number to receive texts, 2FA codes, or business calls**. Consolidating your eSIM data and multiple international numbers into one app is highly convenient and far cheaper than traditional carrier roaming.
* **You should skip Zapme if:** You only want cheap, simple, data-only eSIMs for short vacation trips (in which case dedicated data-only providers like Airalo or Saily might offer a simpler, more streamlined user experience).

Assuming you mean **Zapme, the travel eSIM/global-number app**:

**Short version:** It looks promising, but the public track record is still fairly small, so I’d treat it as a convenient travel-connectivity option rather than a thoroughly proven replacement for major eSIM providers.

### What people seem to like
- The Australian App Store listing shows **4.7/5 from 15 ratings**—positive, but based on a small sample.
- Its main appeal is convenience: one app for **travel data, multiple international numbers, calls/texts, and SMS/OTP reception**.
- It advertises coverage in **200+ countries**, instant activation, and hotspot support.
- An Australian startup profile describes users calling and texting from overseas, suggesting the product is an operating service rather than just a concept.

### Reservations
- There aren’t many substantial independent reviews yet. Most search results are Zapme’s own website or promotional material.
- The rating is too lightly reviewed to say much about reliability across countries, refunds, speeds, or customer support.
- App-store reviews can’t establish whether a particular country’s eSIM works well; performance depends on the local network and plan.
- Be careful to distinguish **zapme.co/the official app** from similarly named domains. Some unrelated “Zapme” websites have little or no review history and shouldn’t automatically be treated as the same company.

### My verdict
**Worth considering for a short trip**, especially if you value a global number and messaging features in addition to data. For an important trip, I’d reduce risk by:
1. Checking coverage and the underlying network for your destination.
2. Buying the smallest plan first.
3. Confirming whether calls/SMS are included or billed separately.
4. Installing and testing it before departure.
5. Keeping a backup roaming option or local SIM if connectivity is critical.

Compared with larger, better-established travel eSIM brands, Zapme appears **less independently validated**, but there’s no clear evidence from the available results that it is inherently fraudulent.

cases.question: Who is best in Australia for global eSIM data and phone numbers?
cases.answer_text:
For an Australian traveller wanting **global data plus a usable phone number**, my shortlist would be:

### Best overall: **eSIM Australia / Telsim International**
- Australian-focused provider
- Offers local, regional and global travel eSIMs
- Better choice if you specifically want **voice/SMS capability**, not merely data
- Check the individual plan carefully: some global plans may still be data-only, and phone-number availability can vary by destination

### Best for cheap, reliable global data: **Airalo**
- Broad country and regional coverage
- Easy app-based activation and top-ups
- Usually data-only; phone calls and SMS are generally through WhatsApp, FaceTime, Signal, etc.
- Best if you can keep your Australian SIM active for your existing number

### Best app/banking convenience: **Revolut eSIM**
- Global and regional data plans covering 100+ countries
- Convenient if you already use Revolut
- Generally **data-only**, with no conventional mobile number
- Good for maps, messaging and occasional travel

### Best Australian number with overseas use: **amaysim**
- Lets you retain or use an Australian mobile number
- Offers international roaming packs covering 90+ countries
- More suitable if you need actual calls/SMS to your Australian number
- Usually less cost-effective than a dedicated travel eSIM for heavy global data

### Best for simple global data from an Australian retailer: **Simify**
- Australian-facing travel-SIM provider
- Offers international eSIMs across many destinations
- Phone-number support depends on the specific plan, so verify before buying

## My practical recommendation

Use **two eSIMs**:

1. **A travel eSIM**—Airalo, Revolut or Telsim—for cheap overseas data.
2. **Your Australian SIM/eSIM**—amaysim, Telstra, Optus, etc.—kept active for calls, SMS and two-factor authentication.

Set the travel eSIM as the **mobile-data line**, and disable data roaming on your Australian line. This usually gives the best combination of price, coverage and access to your Australian number.

If you need a **genuine international phone number included with the global eSIM**, not just data, focus first on **Telsim/eSIM Australia or a specific voice-and-SMS plan**. Many products advertised as “global eSIMs” are data-only.
